title: Health cover for living abroad: travel medical insurance, international health insurance or a membership? Nomad Essential, Nomad Complete and Nomad Citizen compared
summary: Travel medical insurance, international health insurance or a membership? How Nomad Essential, Nomad Complete and Nomad Citizen differ, and how to choose by ...
body_markdown:
If you've been abroad for a while on a travel insurance plan you bought for a trip, maybe you've wondered whether it would pay for anything other than an emergency. The answer depends on the kind of coverage you have, and people living abroad have a few kinds to choose from. This guide explains them and where SafetyWing's three Nomad products,[Nomad Essential](https://safetywing.com/nomad-insurance) ,[Nomad Complete](https://explore.safetywing.com/nomad-insurance-complete) and[Nomad Citizen](https://safetywing.com/nomad-citizen) , fit among them.


## Which kinds of coverage do people living abroad use?


Local insurance is often only available to residents once they’ve registered there, so it tends to suit people who have settled. Eligibility rules differ from place to place, so check them with the insurer or the local health authority. Some credit cards also include travel cover, but it's tied to trips, so check your card's terms for how long a trip it covers and what it pays for before you rely on it for a long stay.


Private insurance is a different story, and SafetyWing offers international coverage on three levels: basic travel medical insurance (Nomad Essential), health insurance that covers routine care as well as your travels (Nomad Complete) and a truly all-in-one membership that covers your income, travels, and healthcare (Nomad Citizen).


## Travel medical insurance: Nomad Essential


Nomad Essential covers new, unexpected illness and injury while you travel, and you can buy it before you leave or after you've already left. It's billed every 4 weeks for up to 364 days at a time, which is why it suits people who are moving and don't know where they'll be in six months. And if you’re traveling for less than a month, you have the option to pick your exact travel dates and cover only those.


- **What it covers:** Hospital care and outpatient care (anything outside hospitalization, like a doctor's visit, a pharmacy, an X-ray or stitches) for new, unexpected issues, up to a US$250,000 overall limit. Medical evacuation, emergency dental up to US$1,000, trip interruption, travel delay and lost checked luggage are included too.


- **Where it works:** 180+ countries. US coverage is extra, and cover in your home country is limited to 30 days (or 90 days if you paid upfront for 364 days of coverage).


- **What it doesn't cover:** Routine and preventive care, maternity and cancer treatment.


- **Price:** From US$62.72 per 4 weeks for ages 18 to 39. Paying upfront for 364 days comes with a 10% discount.


Nomad Essential fits when you're on a trip, even a long one. It isn't meant to be your everyday health plan, so consider that before you buy.


## International health insurance: Nomad Complete


Nomad Complete is global private health insurance designed to be your primary cover (the plan you use for everyday healthcare, not only emergencies) while you live abroad, and it works in your country of residence too. If you'd see a doctor for a check-up, a therapist, or a scan that isn't an emergency, this is the plan for that.


- **Routine care:** Preventive care up to US$350 and outpatient care up to US$5,000.


- **Mental health:** 10 visits a year, within the outpatient limit.


- **Maternity:** Up to US$2,500, after a 10-month waiting period (so it needs planning well ahead).


- **Cancer testing and treatment:** Covered, up to the US$1.5M annual limit.


- **Where it works:** 175 countries, with no restrictions in your home country. If you’re a Hong Kong or Singapore resident, or want to spend up to 6 months in the US, you’ll need the worldwide add-on.


- **Travel protection:** Everything Nomad Essential includes, plus trip cancellation, stolen belongings and burglary.


- **How it's bought:** A 12-month commitment, renewable indefinitely, with sign-up until age 64. Applications take up to 10 days to process, and coverage starts on the 1st or 15th of the month, whichever comes sooner.


- **Price:** US$177.50 per month for ages 18 to 39, US$253.50 per month for ages 40-49, US$380.50 per month for ages 50-59, and US$681.50 per month for ages 60+.


Neither Nomad Essential nor Nomad Complete covers pre-existing conditions. Each plan defines the term differently. On Nomad Essential, it's a condition you had treatment, advice, medication changes or symptoms for in the 180 days before your start date. On Nomad Complete, it's anything you've ever been diagnosed with or treated for, or had symptoms of in the last two years. Nomad Complete covers a lot more than Nomad Essential, but this exclusion applies to both plans.


## Full-suite membership: Nomad Citizen


Nomad Citizen covers your health, income, and travels in one plan, plus a community, for freelancers, founders and families who live without a primary residency, so you have one safety net instead of a separate policy for each risk.


- **Health:** A US$1.5M annual limit covering routine and emergency care and treatment for ongoing covered conditions, with full support for cancer and dialysis. Mental health is covered for up to 15 visits a year. Maternity care is up to US$4,500 for delivery and postnatal care, after a 1-year waiting period. Vision (up to US$500), dental (up to US$1,500) and preventive care (up to US$500) are included.


- **Income protection:** Up to US$4,000 a month if you lose a job or a contract, can't work through illness, or take parental leave. These benefits have waiting periods of 1 to 3 years depending on the benefit, so you can't claim them as soon as you join.


- **Travel and life:** Lost luggage, trip interruption, stolen belongings, evacuation from local unrest, term life and burial cover.


- **Membership extras:** Member events, an expert network, and a SafetyWing card that pays covered medical expenses up to US$500 at the point of care.


- **Who can join:** You need to be 18 to 55, earning at least US$4,000 a month when you apply, and planning to spend at least 6 months of the year outside your home or passport country. A brief medical screening checks that you aren't planning or undergoing significant treatment. The insurance is offered to members of sponsoring organizations such as Plumia, a non-profit working on global mobility. If you're older than 55, or your income is below the threshold when you apply, Nomad Complete is the better route to everyday health cover. The[Nomad Citizen FAQ](https://safetywing.com/nomad-citizen/faq) has the full eligibility rules and waiting periods.


- **Price:** US$443 per month for ages 18 to 39, on a 12-month commitment. Ages 40 to 49 are US$665 and ages 50 to 55 are US$875.


Prices and limits above were last verified on safetywing.com on 29 October 2026.


## Which of the three fits your situation?


Nomad Essential is billed every 4 weeks with options for shorter and more flexible commitment while Nomad Complete and Nomad Citizen are both 12-month commitments, so how long you'll be away narrows the choice quickly. Here are three situations, each matched with the plan that fits:


- **Essential in action:** You're leaving in three weeks for five months of travel, then heading home. You want hospital and emergency cover without a long commitment. Nomad Essential is enough here, and you can buy it after you've already left if you forget.


- **Complete in action:** You've moved somewhere you expect to stay for years, and you want a GP, a dentist and mental health support alongside hospital cover. Nomad Complete is the fit.


- **Citizen in action:** You freelance, have no primary residency, and your income depends on a handful of clients, so you want cover for lost income as well as medical bills. Nomad Citizen fits, if you meet the eligibility requirements.


If you're applying for a digital nomad visa, many countries ask for a minimum coverage limit and for routine and hospital care, which travel medical insurance doesn't include. Each visa has its own rules, so check the official government or immigration website before you buy, because we can't guarantee that any plan will be accepted.
